source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 13 (printed page 22): the twelve end-of-chapter exercises of Chapter 2. Questions here ask what each printed exercise asks, using only the text on this page.

questions.question: Exercise 1 asks learners to discuss how classification systems have:
options: Been replaced by one universal system
Undergone several changes over a period of time
questions.explanation: Exercise 1 asks learners to discuss how classification systems have undergone several changes over a period of time.
questions.source_text: Discuss how classification systems have undergone several changes over a period of time?

questions.question: Exercise 2 asks for two economically important uses of which two groups?
questions.explanation: Exercise 2 asks for two economically important uses of (a) heterotrophic bacteria and (b) archaebacteria.
questions.source_text: State two economically important uses of: (a) heterotrophic bacteria (b) archaebacteria

questions.question: Exercise 3 asks about the nature of the cell walls in which organisms?
questions.explanation: Exercise 3 asks: What is the nature of cell-walls in diatoms?
questions.source_text: What is the nature of cell-walls in diatoms?

questions.question: Exercise 4 asks learners to find out what the terms signify:
questions.explanation: Exercise 4 asks learners to find out what the terms 'algal bloom' and 'red-tides' signify.
questions.source_text: Find out what do the terms ‘algal bloom’ and ‘red-tides’ signify.

questions.question: Exercise 5 asks how which two agents differ?
questions.explanation: Exercise 5 asks: How are viroids different from viruses?
questions.source_text: How are viroids different from viruses?

questions.question: Exercise 6 asks for a brief description of:
options: The four major groups of Protozoa
The four classes of Kingdom Fungi
questions.explanation: Exercise 6 asks learners to describe briefly the four major groups of Protozoa.
questions.source_text: Describe briefly the four major groups of Protozoa.

questions.question: Exercise 7 states that plants are autotrophic and asks for examples of plants that are:
questions.explanation: Exercise 7 asks learners to think of plants that are partially heterotrophic.
questions.source_text: Plants are autotrophic. Can you think of some plants that are partially heterotrophic?

questions.question: Exercise 8 asks what the terms signify:
questions.explanation: Exercise 8 asks: What do the terms phycobiont and mycobiont signify?
questions.source_text: What do the terms phycobiont and mycobiont signify?

questions.question: Exercise 9 asks for a comparative account of the classes of Kingdom Fungi under which headings?
questions.explanation: Exercise 9 lists (i) mode of nutrition and (ii) mode of reproduction.
questions.source_text: (i) mode of nutrition (ii) mode of reproduction

questions.question: Exercise 10 asks for the characteristic features of:
questions.explanation: Exercise 10 asks: What are the characteristic features of Euglenoids?
questions.source_text: What are the characteristic features of Euglenoids?

questions.question: Exercise 11 asks for a brief account of viruses regarding their structure and nature of genetic material, and for naming how many common viral diseases?
questions.explanation: Exercise 11 asks learners to also name four common viral diseases.
questions.source_text: Also name four common viral diseases.

questions.question: Exercise 12 asks learners to organise a class discussion on the topic:
options: Are lichens one organism or two?
questions.explanation: Exercise 12 asks learners to organise a class discussion on whether viruses are living or non-living.
questions.source_text: Organise a discussion in your class on the topic

questions.question: Which exercise question asks learners to 'find out' the meaning of terms?
questions.explanation: Only Exercise 4 begins with 'Find out what do the terms'.
questions.source_text: Find out what do the terms

questions.question: Which of the following topics are the subject of questions in this exercise set?
questions.explanation: Exercises 6, 10, 8 and 5 cover these topics. Alternation of generations and binomial nomenclature are not asked.
questions.source_text: Describe briefly the four major groups of Protozoa. ... What are the characteristic features of Euglenoids? ... What do the terms phycobiont and mycobiont signify? ... How are viroids different from viruses?

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. Exercise 7 concerns plants that are partially heterotrophic.
2. Exercise 3 concerns the cell walls of diatoms.
3. Exercise 10 asks about the structure of bacteriophages.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 match the printed exercises. Exercise 10 asks about the characteristic features of Euglenoids, not bacteriophages.
questions.source_text: Can you think of some plants that are partially heterotrophic? ... What is the nature of cell-walls in diatoms? ... What are the characteristic features of Euglenoids?
